suites.name: durable-watches
suites.intro: Disposable candidate workers and throwaway channels only; never publish credentials or private receipts.

rows.check: Real Slack, Discord and Telegram watch cursors
rows.how: On a disposable candidate, configure real bots in throwaway allowed channels. In an owner chat request one matching-message watch per connector, confirm the worker and scope, and record watch/event/cursor IDs privately. Send a nonmatching message and then matching messages. Restart only the candidate after checkpoint and repeat a poll. For Slack exercise a multi-page backlog; for Discord use more than 100 messages. Revoke each grant, then pause and stop all watches. For Telegram compare a duplicate received message ID with a second distinct ID. Interrupt candidate journal persistence, verify the receiver holds its update acknowledgement until commit and resumes without loss. While a Telegram turn is still running, answer its destructive-action approval and send a message in another allowed chat; verify polling dispatches both before the original turn goes idle. Record the receiver-downtime limitation rather than claiming chat-history recovery.
rows.pass_when: Idle/nonmatching polls make no model calls, matching messages report once across restart/pages, saved progress advances over nonmatches, channel restrictions and revocation fail closed, and Pause/Stop prevent new reports. Telegram replay covers only durably received updates; no real connector smoke is claimed without private producing-path receipts.
rows.past_bug: #554: declared messaging triggers had no replayable watch producer.

rows.check: Always-on placement and fenced two-worker cursor hand-over
rows.how: Use two disposable candidates named DesktopWorker and ServerWorker with network device IDs distinct from their installation IDs. From an owner chat on DesktopWorker create a schedule watch with ServerWorker available; inspect the named confirmation and executing row. Stop only the disposable creator and observe a server-side event/report. Bring it back, verify list/Pause/Stop through peer controls, set and clear the owner preference, and try an unavailable designated worker. Move a second watch with pending observations after all in-flight deliveries finish; interrupt once after destination import before acknowledgement, retry the same move, and compare cursor, event IDs, budget history and source fencing. Start the reverse move from the destination worker and verify that the original source receipt is complete and the returned watch executes once. Never restart production workers.
rows.pass_when: Default chooses the server; explicit override and synced preference win, unavailable preference never silently falls back. Events continue with creator offline. Source is fenced before import, cursor/outbox IDs and cost history survive hand-over without duplicate reports, and synced display rows never execute. Remote active-creator turns and Telegram journal migration remain explicit follow-ups, not passing claims.
rows.past_bug: #555: watches were pinned to the creating worker and had no default placement.

suites.name: two-worker-smoke
suites.intro: Run before a release (never on a schedule) from the ServerWorker worker with DesktopWorker online; swap roles for a second pass when both are available. Each check maps to a bug the owner previously found by hand (session titles in brackets).

rows.check: Unified generation named-choice safety, quotes and catalog shape
rows.how: Use disposable account preferences and throwaway chats on two candidate workers; never alter the owner's choices or caps. Remember a fal choice for each tested kind, then make unattended calls through that kind's tool naming SuperGrok or a different fal model. Inspect catalog/submission logs. For matching probes use a declared endpoint priced above the confirmation threshold, never approve a paid retry, and call runFalModel from worker A with the kind's remembered fal choice pinned to worker B, then with its worker omitted. Run default searchModels and searchModels(source=supergrok) with a real subscription account. Compare searchModels for kling/v4/text-to-video with its default choice-card and interactive generateVideo quotes. With the same SuperGrok account on both workers, request choices from each and inspect holders. Compare compact and full_schema searchModels for a large fal schema including generate_audio. Save an unpriced model, then an unavailable-holder choice, through the choices API and inspect the warning and save latency. Archive throwaway chats and discard only disposable preferences.
rows.pass_when: Unattended names that differ from a remembered choice skip with named_choice_differs_from_stored before any catalog lookup or submission. Matching runFalModel calls reach the existing price/confirmation/cap decision on the remembered holder, without injecting worker A or switching sources; above-threshold probes skip without billing. Default and SuperGrok-filtered searchModels return subscription options and their allowed values without errors. The single search quote, choice card and generate quote show the same known default price (0.785 USD for the recorded Kling rate; use the current provider rate if changed). Each source/account/model/options tuple appears once, preferring the local holder, and different accounts/options remain separate. Default searchModels JSON is at most 32768 ASCII-escaped characters, truncation is explicit, full_schema returns the complete schema, and generate_audio stays boolean. An unpriced save returns stored_choice_unpriced and a skip warning; unavailable or timed-out quotes retain their error and return stored_choice_unavailable within the two-second quote budget. The pick is saved in both cases. No paid retry is approved. Missing provider/worker evidence is not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #512 silently replaced named unattended sources with stored choices; #513 masked prices and misreported unavailable saves; #514 duplicated holders, returned huge schemas and typed booleans as files. Review also caught subscription-schema crashes and runFalModel overriding remembered holders.

rows.check: Worker identity
rows.how: GET deploy-status
rows.pass_when: both workers listed by name (not a hex id), revisions shown
rows.past_bug: ServerWorker shows as a bunch of numbers

rows.check: Subagent on the other worker
rows.how: a local session starts a background subagent on the peer, messages it after it finishes (resume), then starts and stops a second one
rows.pass_when: Task, SendMessage and TaskStop all used; reply SUBAGENT-DONE
rows.past_bug: subagents on another worker could not be messaged, stopped or resumed

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: keep every subagent prompt tiny. 1) Use Task with worker "{peer}" and mode background to start any coding subagent from your roster with the prompt "reply with the single word SUB-OK, no tools". 2) When it reports, use SendMessage to that agent with "reply with the single word SUB-AGAIN, no tools" and wait for its report. 3) Use Task with worker "{peer}" and mode background again with the prompt "run sleep 300 in Bash", then stop it at once with TaskStop. Then reply with just: SUBAGENT-DONE

rows.check: Message as the turn ends
rows.how: send a second message the moment the first reply appears
rows.pass_when: two user bubbles, one ONE reply and one TWO reply (nothing lost, nothing doubled)
rows.past_bug: a message sent as a turn ended was lost or shown twice

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word ONE and use no tools.
Reply with the single word TWO and use no tools.

rows.check: Prompt card in an open chat
rows.how: open a chat through the preview port; ask it to use AskUserQuestion with two options
rows.pass_when: the card renders in the open chat, an answer reaches the turn
rows.past_bug: prompt cards did not appear in an already-open chat

rows.check: Compact
rows.how: one reply, then /compact through the API, then one more reply
rows.pass_when: compact boundary recorded, the next message still answers
rows.past_bug: /compact failed or lost the session

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word OK and use no tools.
Reply with the single word AGAIN and use no tools.

rows.check: Image edit on the configured provider
rows.how: editImage on a 4x4 PNG the runner writes (one paid image call)
rows.pass_when: editImage used; reply EDITED
rows.past_bug: image edit failed on the configured provider

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: use the editImage tool once on the image at {image} with the prompt "make it red". Then reply with just: EDITED

rows.check: Desktop quit and restart
rows.how: owner quits the desktop app on the peer and starts it again
rows.pass_when: the peer comes back online and its sessions open from this worker
rows.past_bug: desktop app did not come back cleanly after quit

rows.check: Android voice call lock and unlock
rows.how: On a physical phone running the branch APK and a worker serving the branch UI, start a GPT Live call in a throwaway chat. Lock for 10 seconds, unlock, and speak again. Repeat after rotating the phone while locked and after changing system light/dark mode. Archive the throwaway chat after ending the call. Capture adb logcat for activity recreation or renderer loss and the worker voice/SSE logs.
rows.pass_when: The same call hears and replies after each unlock; no audio close with code 1006, cold from_seq=0 feed connection, activity recreation or WebView renderer loss during the cycle.
rows.past_bug: #1969: locking kept voice alive but unlocking destroyed the page and audio socket

rows.check: Changed worker install id
rows.how: On disposable paired workers only, restore one worker's device keys into a fresh data directory with a new install id. Wait for its signed presence to reach the peer; pick it for a chat and read its Git state. Join a third disposable worker and confirm it waits for fresh signed presence before resolving the new id. Do not change live worker identities.
rows.pass_when: the peer resolves the new install id to the original device, names it correctly and routes chat/Git control there; the certificate's old id still works; a snapshot alone never authorizes the second alias
rows.past_bug: #1716: a stale membership install id made peer-side lookups miss an active worker

rows.check: Delegated Claude preview and sidebar
rows.how: start an owner Claude session on each worker; ask it to open the running UI using the preview link in its workspace facts, without reading key files; wait for the sidebar data to load
rows.pass_when: both sessions receive a working session-bound link; the desktop link uses loopback; the preview lists the same visible active chats and agents as the owner's UI (Active counts chats, not links or hidden workers)
rows.past_bug: #1789: delegated sessions received no preview link; desktop links named an unreachable LAN address; an initial Active 0 needed tracing

rows.check: Offline restart transcript delta (#1978)
rows.how: On disposable workers only: sync a chat with 100 events, take its peer offline, restart the owner, append 400 events while its outbox is held, then bring the peer back. Repeat with reversed dial direction. Open Settings > Devices > This worker during catch-up. Also repeat from a backup whose stream head is behind the peer.
rows.pass_when:
The 400-event delta arrives on first safe contact in seconds, with no historical republish, seven 64-or-fewer-event receiver batches and ordered seq 1..500. Devices shows Syncing during apply and Ready afterwards. A restored owner keeps the hold until signed rollback proof is 
... [74101 chars truncated] ...
synthetic history, never an installed worker or its database. On that disposable receiver run python -m app.maintenance.history_indexing --apply; without this opt-in confirm no history migration starts. Let its concurrent index migration finish, then move a large synthetic chat while another named throwaway chat appends messages and searches a unique live marker. Inspect per-table timings, WAL and single-row latency. Confirm moved text can still be viewed while its history_index_state is pending. Restart only the disposable receiver part-way through catch-up. After catch-up, recall and session-list search must find native, delegated and mirrored markers including punctuation, literal percent/underscore and Unicode. Also move a legacy away-mode chat whose reminder exists only in a user node; check inheritance before catch-up. Repeat the concurrent migration with about one million synthetic events and a live writer. Remove only these disposable resources.

Moves do not synchronously maintain history GIN indexes; live messages remain searchable and do not inherit a shared GIN pending-list backlog. Both live and caught-up history search plans use their separate partial indexes, history GIN pending lists are separate and bounded to 1 MiB, and live edits move back to state 0, pending work resumes after restart without missing or duplicate hits, and away-mode inheritance reads pending history. Migration uses concurrent builds, short lock acquisition, preserves source row counts and does not rewrite the event heap. Record actual time, WAL, corpus shape and live insert latency; an unrun worker path is not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #295: bulk hand-off GIN maintenance stalled imports and live writes; a larger shared pending list moved the delay onto live chats.

rows.check: Generation preferences can be read and edited in conversation without submission
rows.how: In a disposable owner account/chat on the candidate revision, enable app-config tools. Ask generationPreferences to read image picks, then acknowledge remembering an exact discovered source/account/model/worker with declared options. Read it back through the tool and GET /generation/choices; on the next turn check the production run context binding without submitting generation. Repeat for a paused disposable automation created through createAutomation, using its returned auto-* job_id and GET /generation/jobs/{id}/choices. Forget both after acknowledgment, read back, and archive only the disposable chat/job. Do not call any provider or change real owner preferences.
rows.pass_when: The authenticated owner namespace matches the choices API and next-turn production binding; get, remember and forget accept the real auto-* automation ID; job picks are pinned and isolated from remembered picks and favourites. Missing acknowledgment, non-admin calls, malformed picks and unknown job IDs do not write. The tool explicitly says saving does not verify availability or approve spending. No provider submission, reservation, charge or screenshot occurs.
rows.past_bug: #379: remembered/job choices had HTTP/card writers but no dedicated conversational read/edit tool.

rows.check: Real automation IDs accept pinned generation choices
rows.how: On a disposable worker, POST an automation; save/read/clear its job choice.
rows.pass_when: auto-* ID works; a dry run binds the pick; API-user access is denied.
rows.past_bug: #558: UUID validation rejected every app-created automation ID.

rows.check: Legacy projectless owners gain the coordination ceiling and attach action
rows.how: On a disposable candidate worker only, prepare synthetic old-version owner sessions with NULL and literal code modes, no project, and a short transcript. Include project-bound, API, worker, automation and foreign-principal controls. Upgrade and restart twice, then sync additional NULL/code rows from a synthetic old-version peer after startup has completed. For both a native provider and delegated Claude, resume each owner chat and inspect the real options/tool registry: read a registered-project file, request a shell or project write, then attach a disposable project while idle and send another turn. Never modify an installed worker database or publish private receipts.
rows.pass_when: Both restarts and later peer upserts preserve transcripts and identity controls. Ordinary projectless owner rows store chat, expose Attach project without a Git panel, permit registered-project reads and refuse shell/Edit/Write/Python with StartSession(project=...) guidance. Project-bound controls retain their checkout/full tools; API, worker, automation and foreign-principal policy is unchanged. Attach keeps history, resets access to Ask and restores the project surface on the next real turn. Record actual provider/tool and UI evidence; unexecuted upgrade steps are not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #553: deferred mode migration left legacy projectless owners on the code surface.

rows.check: Offline database work outlives ordinary SQL deadlines
rows.how: Disposable: large-history upgrade, maintenance, dump/restore and rollback.
rows.pass_when: Work finishes; maintenance is bounded; ordinary SQL limits return.
rows.past_bug: #580 review: short server defaults could cancel every boot migration.

rows.check: Named scenario ID survives a real worker run and persisted result
rows.how: On a disposable preview worker only, run python -m scripts.live_smoke run --preview --url <preview-url> --rows harness-basics.named-id-result-round-trip --results-dir <scratch-results>. Inspect the result file printed by the CLI and confirm the throwaway session was archived. Never target an installed worker or overwrite release evidence.
rows.pass_when: The worker replies OK, the CLI exits successfully, and the persisted result contains exactly the selected named row with id harness-basics.named-id-result-round-trip and status pass, without a numeric replacement. The partial run remains marked partial and its throwaway session is archived. A missing result-file or cleanup inspection is not a pass.
rows.past_bug: #521: parallel additions reused numeric IDs; named replacements need end-to-end execution and persisted-result coverage on a real worker.

steps.prompt: Live test {run}: reply with the single word OK and use no tools.

rows.check: Native generation aliases cannot bypass unified admission
rows.how: On a disposable candidate worker with synthetic data and an already configured verified subscription, create throwaway native chat and automation sessions permitting only GenerateNativeImage and GenerateNativeVideo. Do not enter credentials or approve a paid submission. With no remembered/job pick, call each alias and inspect its structured result and provider-request logs. Repeat with an unreadable synthetic job choice, then a valid saved choice and an already-exceeded synthetic daily cap. Check image Included pricing and the exact verified video estimate. Archive only the throwaway sessions. Run the focused no-provider registry tests for the approved confirmation retry; never use this smoke row to authorize a real generation charge.
rows.pass_when: Both interactive aliases return choose with the unified price/choice envelope; both unattended aliases skip without a saved choice or with unreadable choices. A valid saved choice still refuses an exhausted cap, including Included images, with zero provider submissions. Above-threshold calls require the unified one-use confirmation receipt before reserve/submission. Exact approved retries and job choices are covered by the no-provider test. Alias choice-card rendering is tracked separately and must not be inferred from JSON alone.
rows.past_bug: #545: raw native registrations submitted without resolver admission or generation_budget.reserve.

rows.check: Native owner approval retains its caller scope
rows.how: On disposable native candidate + #535, park and approve the same offline call.
rows.pass_when: Main rerun uses its pass once; another agent session needs its own yes.
rows.past_bug: #559: CLI identity plumbing must not change native approval scope.

rows.check: Detected owner identity reaches fresh native and delegated chats
rows.how: Disposable worker: detect Ada; Recall in fresh chats; Remember Grace; redetect.
rows.pass_when: Grace wins; no duplicates or addresses; Git author stays unchanged.
rows.past_bug: #556: account detection did not feed ordinary owner memory.

rows.check: PostgreSQL finishes a dirty FAST shutdown under bounded write pressure
rows.how: Use only a disposable candidate container and synthetic volumes, never a live worker or database. Give Docker 120 seconds of stop grace. Run the checkpoint lab's two same-volume writers (each overwrites 32 MiB and fsyncs for at most 240 seconds), create and update its 32768-row checkpoint_probe table, and stop the container while both writers remain active. Repeat three times. Record checkpoint write/sync/total durations, container exit status and the next startup's recovery log; verify every committed row after restart. Separately inject a stuck postmaster only in a disposable fixture to exercise the 60-second deadline fence.
rows.pass_when: All three dirty shutdowns finish cleanly within the 60-second PostgreSQL budget and 120-second container grace, with pressure still active, no forced-stop failure and no crash recovery on restart. Committed rows survive. A stuck postmaster is still forcibly stopped and reported as a failure with recovery descriptors retained; exceeding the real deadline is never skipped as a lab precondition.
rows.past_bug: #533: the 30-second FAST deadline killed a shutdown checkpoint that needed slightly longer under same-volume fsync pressure.

rows.check: Turn finish survives brief DB pool exhaustion
rows.how: Disposable candidate only: finish 45 real sessions under >2s pool pressure.
rows.pass_when: All finish; leases renew; UI stays live; one pool stats log per burst.
rows.past_bug: #580: a 2s acquisition timeout became a failed worker ResultMessage.

rows.check: Pytest teardown reports a late basetemp writer without losing the result
rows.how: In a disposable candidate checkout on each worker, run PYTHONPATH=fluid pytest tests/scripts/test_local_ci_stages.py::test_kill_mid_stage_resumes_from_the_heartbeat tests/scripts/test_test_scratch.py -o addopts= -q. The crash regression checks that its heartbeat writer stops and signal handlers are restored without releasing the crash receipt. The late-writer regression starts a real child to refill basetemp between the cleanup scan and rmdir, once and repeatedly, for passing and failing child sessions. Do not restart the installed app or clean unrelated scratch.
rows.pass_when: All scratch regressions pass. A transient refill that is removed within three retries warns and preserves the child's own test exit status. A persistent leftover still makes the child session fail, even when all its tests passed. Diagnostics identify the owner and bounded leftover entries; an available ownership receipt is restored for the reaper. Receipt or listing errors are reported without replacing the original cleanup failure. Serial, xdist, explicit basetemp and standalone Fluid ownership checks still pass.
rows.past_bug: #570: backend-security passed every test then exited 1 when a directory refilled during pytest session scratch cleanup.

rows.check: Retired home cleanup preserves ordinary identities and spending history
rows.how: On a disposable candidate worker with synthetic legacy account/spend rows, upgrade and inspect agent identities, avatars, owner introduction/memory and Usage limits. Rename an ordinary agent and change its avatar, lower the spending limit, then finish a bounded real coordination job including a remote child when available. Replay its accounting receipt after restart. Delete an ordinary disposable chat and try the retired home/research routes. Keep all receipts private; no screenshots are needed.
rows.pass_when: Ordinary identity edits preserve all unrelated config, avatars and owner memory survive, and cumulative local/remote cost is charged once across restart/replay. No dedicated agent, protected home, home prompt or research runner appears. Retired routes remain unavailable; ordinary chat deletion succeeds. Historical assistant-prefixed shared endpoints still serve their documented owner-only functions until the atomic naming follow-up #561.
rows.past_bug: #557: shared service naming, dead research constants and stale deletion documentation outlived home retirement.

rows.check: Watchdog retains ownership when bounded stop times out
rows.how: On a disposable candidate, gate fsync/source reads; stop/start, release, stop.
rows.pass_when: Stop avoids source I/O, logs 32 frames max, retains ownership and rejoins.
rows.past_bug: #547: stop cleared a live thread handle while fsync was blocked.
